title: Progressive variant rollouts and compatibility matrix spec
author: Asha Patel
summary: Specification for progressive model variant rollouts, compatibility gating, and a canonical compatibility matrix used by Redwood’s serving platform to safely release model variants across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
overview:
Background: As Redwood expands model offerings (quantized variants, instruction-tuned checkpoints, and architecture forks), product teams must be able to roll variants to subsets of traffic without risking regressions. This spec defines the gating rules, compatibility matrix, and orchestration primitives that the Redwood platform will provide.

Scope: Applies to model variant rollouts that change any of: tokenizer version, model architecture family (e.g., transformer block changes), KV cache layout, quantization format, or callable tool schemas. Includes Hosted API and Dedicated. Private customers may opt-in to use the same control plane primitives.
goals_and_non_goals:
Goals:
- Provide deterministic compatibility checks that prevent unsafe variant assignment to previously cached KV/embedding workloads.
- Define rollout gates (syntactic, perf, quality) that are enforced automatically for canary and percent-rollouts.
- Expose a concise compatibility matrix for model owners and platform engineers.

Non-goals:
- This spec does not change model training or evaluation pipelines.
- This does not propose new model format standards (that is a separate infra initiative).

requirements:
1) Safety: The platform must block variant assignment when incompatibility risk is detected (e.g., tokenizer mismatch, cache layout change).
2) Observability: Rollout must emit per-variant metrics: latency p50/p95, error rate, per-token cost, and quality deltas on a curated prompt set.
3) Granularity: Support routing by percent, by customer (account_id), and by route (API key + model route).
4) Fallbacks: Automatic, fast fallback to the last-known-good variant on errors or on defined SLO breaches.
5) Compatibility API: A read-only endpoint that returns the compatibility matrix for any model family.
6) Manual override: Admins can create emergency rollbacks with one-click in Console.
7) Private deploy opt-in: Private deployments must be able to opt-out of platform gating while still consuming the compatibility matrix as guidance.
compatibility_matrix:
Compatibility matrix format (canonical):
Columns: variant_id | model_family | tokenizer_version | kv_layout | quant_format | tool_schema_hash | compatible_with_previous_kv (yes/no) | notes
Example rows:
- v1.0.0 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v2 | kv-v1 | fp16 | ts-abc123 | yes | baseline
- v1.1.0-quant | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v2 | kv-v1 | int8-q4 | ts-abc123 | yes | quantized weights; safe for cached prefixes
- v2.0.0 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v3 | kv-v2 | int8-q4 | ts-def456 | no | tokenizer and kv_layout changed; must invalidate prefix cache
- v2.0.1 | redwood-rlhf-7b | tok-v3 | kv-v2 | int8-q4 | ts-def456 | yes | minor patch to cache checksum logic
Access pattern: GET /compatibility/model-family/{family} -> returns list of rows as above. Console will render as table and include links to model-onboarding pages.
design:
High-level design:
1) Compatibility service: A central read-only service (compat-service) stores canonical rows and exposes an HTTP API and internal gRPC API. It is the source of truth for gating.
2) Admission controller: The serving control plane queries compat-service at the time of assignment. If 'compatible_with_previous_kv' is 'no' and assignment would route traffic with cached prefixes, the admission controller either: a) blocks assignment, or b) requires explicit cache invalidation in rollout plan.
3) Rollout engine changes: The rollout engine will add a 'compatibility_check' phase before traffic shifts and during scheduled canary evaluation windows.
4) Metrics pipeline: During canary we evaluate quality using a lightweight prompt set (default 50 prompts) executed asynchronously and compared against a baseline using automatic metrics (perplexity/ROUGE/ROUGE-L/semantic-similarity) and hand-curated business metrics where available.
5) UI: Console shows per-variant compatibility flags, matrix link, and a one-click 'invalidate cache and continue' flow that triggers a controlled cache purge job.
Implementation details:
- compat-service storage: Postgres table with row-level version and 'effective_from' timestamps.
- Atomic rollout changes: Rollout engine persists desired-state in a config store (etcd) and coordinates canaries via leader election.
- Backward-compatibility modes: 'strict' (default) blocks unsafe assignments; 'permissive' allows assignment but will route only to new sessions. Private deployments default to permissive unless configured.
Security considerations:
- compat-service read API is internal-only and authenticated via mTLS.
- Audit logs written to central audit-log store for every variant assignment decision.
api_and_config_examples:
Example compatibility API response (JSON snippet):
[
  {
    "variant_id": "v2.0.0",
    "model_family": "redwood-rlhf-7b",
    "tokenizer_version": "tok-v3",
    "kv_layout": "kv-v2",
    "quant_format": "int8-q4",
    "tool_schema_hash": "ts-def456",
    "compatible_with_previous_kv": "no",
    "notes": "requires prefix invalidation or routing to new sessions only"
  }
]

Rollout config (YAML) example for canary with explicit cache invalidation:
---
rollout_name: rl-7b-v2-canary
model_family: redwood-rlhf-7b
variant: v2.0.0
strategy:
  - step: canary
    percent: 5
    duration_minutes: 60
    compatibility_action: invalidate_prefix_cache
  - step: ramp
    percent: 50
    duration_minutes: 240
    compatibility_action: validate_metrics
  - step: full
    percent: 100
    duration_minutes: 0
    compatibility_action: none
---
CLI: rwdctl rollout create --file rl-7b-v2-canary.yaml
rollout_plan:
Rollout procedure (recommended):
1) Author prepares variant and publishes to model catalog with compatibility rows.
2) Run automated compatibility check: rwdctl compat check --family redwood-rlhf-7b --variant v2.0.0. Address any 'no' flags.
3) Create canary with 'compatibility_action=invalidate_prefix_cache' if necessary.
4) Monitor for 60 minutes primary metrics (latency p95, errors) and run quality prompt set jobs.
5) If quality delta > threshold (see metrics_and_slos), automatically rollback.
6) If stable, continue ramp steps.
7) Post-rollout: create release note entry and pin variant as stable in the catalog.
Edge cases:
- Hot split of dedicated pools: for Dedicated nodes with long-lived sessions, the system prefers session-aware routing to avoid state mismatch.
- Private deployments with permissive mode: an explicit 'force' parameter is required to bypass strict gating.
metrics_and_slos:
Primary SLOs during rollout windows:
- Latency: p95 increase <= 20% relative to baseline or absolute p95 <= 300ms (whichever is tighter per route)
- Errors: 5xx increase <= 0.1 percentage point absolute
- Quality: Semantic-similarity delta on evaluation prompt-set >= -0.03 (cosine sim) OR business-critical prompt pass-rate >= baseline - 2ppt
Rollout thresholds (automatic rollback triggers):
- Any single route exceeds latency SLO for 3 consecutive windows (window = 5 minutes)
- Error delta exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive windows
- Quality probe failure rate > 10% in canary window
Telemetry and storage:
- All per-variant telemetry shall be stored with variant tags for 90 days in metrics store. Prompt-set evaluation artifacts retained for 30 days by default.
operational_playbook:
On-call steps for rollout incidents:
1) Pager triggers: spike in errors or rollout rollback event.
2) Triage: identify variant_id and affected routes with 'rwdctl rollout status --id <id>'.
3) Immediate mitigation: trigger rollout rollback (rwdctl rollout rollback --id <id>) OR trigger emergency fallback policy to baseline variant.
4) If issue is cache incompatibility: run 'rwdctl cache purge --scope=affected-customers --variant <old>' only after coordinating with product to accept transient cold-start costs.
5) Postmortem: owner_team opens a postmortem within 48 hours and tags the rollout with incident id.
6) Prevent recurrence: add additional compatibility unit tests to the model onboarding harness.
rollout_criteria_checklist:
- [ ] Compatibility matrix entry exists for the new variant
- [ ] Automated compat check passes or explicit cache invalidation plan approved
- [ ] Canary prompt-set defined and uploaded
- [ ] SLO thresholds configured for the route
- [ ] Fallback variant tagged and healthy
- [ ] Monitor dashboards pinned and alerting validated
notes_and_next_steps:
Next engineering work: implement compat-service migration script, add 'compatibility_action' to rollout engine, and add Console UI for one-click cache invalidation. Product will schedule an internal pilot with two active customers in Dedicated by Q3 2026.
Open questions:
1) Standardize 'kv_layout' semantic versioning across model-owners.
2) Decide retention for prompt-set results for compliance and debugging.
3) Define default compatibility_policy per region (latency-sensitive regions may prefer permissive mode).
